req.title: Honour Accept: application/json
req.statement: The system shall respect an Accept: application/json request header by serialising responses as JSON.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that when a client sends Accept: application/json, the server must respond with JSON-serialised content. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — standard GET /get with Accept: application/json yields 200 and correct Content-Type; (2) positive EP — POST /post with Accept: application/json yields 200 JSON; (3) positive EP — /headers endpoint with Accept: application/json; (4) negative NEG — endpoint that does not produce JSON (/status/200) still returns 2xx but we verify the Accept header is echoed back correctly; (5) boundary BVA — Accept header with quality values (application/json;q=1.0) still honoured; (6) DT — multiple endpoints cross-checked for JSON content-type; (7) NEG — verifying that the Content-Type in response is exactly 'application/json' not a superset or different type. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 not >=200), exact content-type strings, and exact JSON keys present in payloads.

tests.name: test_get_with_accept_json_returns_200_and_json_content_type
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /get endpoint is available
actions: Send GET /get with Accept: application/json header
expected: Response body is valid JSON containing 'headers' key
trace: R-HTTPBIN-037: system shall respect Accept: application/json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_get_with_accept_json_returns_200_and_json_content_type():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get', headers={'Accept': 'application/json'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    assert ct.startswith('application/json'), f'Expected application/json, got {ct}'
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    assert 'headers' in body
    assert 'url' in body
    assert 'args' in body
    assert 'origin' in body

test_get_with_accept_json_returns_200_and_json_content_type()

from httpbin.core import app

def test_content_type_is_not_text_html_when_accept_json():

tests.name: test_basic_auth_success_with_accept_json_returns_json
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> endpoint is available
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/user/passwd with valid Basic Auth credentials and Accept: application/json
expected: Response body contains authenticated=true and user='user'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-037: /basic-auth endpoint must honour Accept: application/json on success
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
import base64

def test_basic_auth_success_with_accept_json_returns_json():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'user:passwd').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/user/passwd',
        headers={
            'Accept': 'application/json',
            'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'
        }
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    assert ct.startswith('application/json'), f'Expected application/json, got {ct}'
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    assert body.get('authenticated') == True
    assert body.get('user') == 'user'

test_basic_auth_success_with_accept_json_returns_json()

tests.name: test_get_response_body_exact_keys_with_accept_json
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /get endpoint is available
actions: Capture response and parse JSON body
expected: Response JSON has exactly the keys: url, args, headers, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-037: exact payload structure must match when Accept: application/json is sent
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json

def test_get_response_body_exact_keys_with_accept_json():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar', headers={'Accept': 'application/json'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    assert ct.startswith('application/json')
    body = json.loads(r.data)
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == expected_keys, f'Keys mismatch: {set(body.keys())} != {expected_keys}'
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert isinstance(body['url'], str)

test_get_response_body_exact_keys_with_accept_json()
